page: UpCloud GPU-192xCPU-1920GB-8xB200 is a GPU-accelerated server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 CPU architecture with 192 shared virtual CPUs and 1920.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 10.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance does not include local storage, meaning storage resources must be attached externally. It comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

The defining characteristic of this server is its integrated graphics processing hardware. It is equipped with eight NVIDIA B200 GPUs from the Blackwell family. These accelerators provide a combined total of 1536 GB of video RAM (VRAM). This massive pool of high-bandwidth memory is designed to handle extremely large parallel processing workloads directly on the GPU cluster.

Given the presence of eight Blackwell-generation GPUs and a high system memory capacity of nearly two terabytes, this server is designed for massive parallel computing tasks. It is highly suited for large-scale deep learning model training, massive LLM inference, and complex data science simulations. The shared CPU allocation suggests that while the GPU and memory resources are massive and dedicated, the CPU compute layer is shared, which represents a specific architectural tradeoff to optimize resource density and cost efficiency for GPU-bound workloads.
